newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers threaten fur ban.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers threaten fur ban.

text.p: European Union environment ministers threatened on Monday to impose an EU import ban on fur from animals caught in leg-hold traps unless negotiators from Canada, the United States and Russia accept tighter humane trapping standards, a British official told reporters.

The official said ministers, in a closed door meeting, said an existing draft agreement on trapping standards was "completely unacceptable" and said they had asked the European Commission to prepare a ban to start as soon as possible.

Negotiators from the four sides have been in talks for months over improved trapping standards in an effort to avert a fur import ban already agreed by the EU, which delayed implementation while negotiations continued.
The talks aim to lay down standards for traps which kill or catch wild animals such as muskrats, lynx and wolves.

Canada and Russia had accepted the draft deal on trapping standards but the United States thought even that went too far. The EU rejection of the compromise means that all three will have to return to talks to avoid being hit by the threatened ban.
